title: Another Codex session's read-only command (git status) in a worktree with a carried gate refuses the gate's credit: no read-only classification for Codex commands
outcome:
Found by the independent evaluation of w-a450af06e8bd (Codex evaluator delegation-16f984ed-81fd-455c-b2ab-b12c571003e2, evaluation 5bc7bccd9ef84c4f810696e190d65ce9, criterion 1: fail).

engram_session_command_reads_only (src/engram_turn_checks.rs:685) treats only Claude sessions' commands as possibly read-only: `record.session.agent == Agent::Claude && engram_command_reads_only(...)`. engram_command_reads_only uses claude_bash_command_is_read_only, a Bash-syntax classifier.

A Codex session's command, for example `git status --short` run through Codex's exec tool, is therefore always a possible write. When another Codex session runs it in a worktree with a carried gate, the gate's credit is refused. The test another_claude_sessions_read_only_command_in_the_worktree_leaves_the_gate_credited explicitly expects this refusal for a Codex `git status`.

Codex on Windows runs commands through PowerShell, so classifying them needs a fail-closed PowerShell read-only checker that unwraps Codex's shell invocation. w-61ca4952467c ("Implement a fail-closed PowerShell read-only reviewer command checker") is the likely prerequisite.
acceptance: A Codex command the classifier cannot prove read-only still refuses the credit and the refusal line names it; a test covers it.

A provably read-only command (for example git status, git log, a file read) run by another Codex session in a worktree with a carried gate does not refuse the gate's credit, judged by a fail-closed classifier of Codex's command form on Windows; a test covers it.
